name: Account Menu
description: A household account menu with an identity header, product items, and distinct app and SSO sign-out actions.
usage:
<AccountMenu
  user={{ name: 'Avery Chen', email: 'avery@example.com' }}
  items={[{ id: 'sessions', label: 'Active sessions', onSelect: () => undefined }]}
  appSignOut={{ label: 'Sign out of Photos', onSelect: () => undefined }}
  ssoSignOut={{ label: 'Sign out everywhere', onSelect: () => undefined }}
/>

anatomy.description: Compact avatar button named after the signed-in user.
Name and email block that anchors the menu to an account.
Caller-defined account actions such as active sessions or settings.
Distinct app-session and SSO sign-out items with product-supplied labels.

dos: Label both sign-out actions by product so sessions stay distinguishable.
Keep the identity header even when there are no product items.
Order neutral account items before the sign-out actions.
donts: Don't merge app and SSO sign-out into one ambiguous action.
Don't show the menu on public surfaces with no signed-in identity.
Don't bury primary navigation here; it is for account and session actions.

examples.title: Household account
examples.description: Sign-out actions are labeled by the product so people can tell an application session from the shared SSO session.

examples.title: Without product items
examples.description: The items list is optional; the identity header and sign-out actions remain.

guidance.useWhen: A signed-in household identity needs session and account actions.
guidance.avoidWhen: The surface has no identity concept or is public.
guidance.behavior: App-session and SSO sign-out stay distinct actions with product-supplied labels.
guidance.responsive: The trigger stays a compact avatar so it fits top bars at any width.

keyboard.action: Opens the account menu from the avatar trigger.
Moves the highlight through the items and sign-out actions.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the avatar trigger.

notes: Implements the dropdown menu pattern through the Radix primitive; the trigger is named after the signed-in user.
App-session and SSO sign-out are distinct items with product-supplied labels, so the scope of each is announced.
The identity header is presentational text inside the menu, not an actionable item.
